jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Indiana, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Indiana, or search an address, to see every civic district that covers it — county, township, city or town, school district, ZIP code, both General Assembly chambers and the U.S. House — with the district's own identity on each card.
jsonld.keywords: Indiana district map, what district am I in, Indiana Senate district, Indiana House district, county lookup, civic districts, who represents me

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Indiana, and who represents you there.

head.title: Indiana district lookup — districtry Indiana
head.description: Tap the map or search an Indiana address: county, Indiana Senate and House, U.S. House district — and the districts that cover it. Free, no login.
head.og_description: Every civic district that covers a point in Indiana.
head.og_image_alt: districtry Indiana — every district that covers a point.
head.twitter_description: Click or search an Indiana address to see every district that covers it.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 9 congressional districts — the largest districts Indiana carries below the state apart from the Court of Appeals' three

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app. The layer's own district field is CD120; 9 features for Indiana, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Indiana Senate District
layers.rank_note: 50 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Indiana Senate district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (state upper chamber, field SLDU), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 50 features, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: NO ROSTER SHIPS IN THIS CHANGE, and the card says so: it names the district and links the General Assembly's own member directory rather than naming a senator this instance has not fetched. Recorded as gap in-general-assembly-roster; the Open States export lands in its own change with its own weekly workflow, the route every other instance took.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 92 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

source.answers: Which county contains the point, and who won each seat on its board of commissioners and its county council.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 92 features, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: Every commissioner and county council member in 91 of the 92 counties, each the winner of that seat's most recent election in the Indiana Election Division's certified results (the 2022 and 2024 generals), dated to that election and rebuilt weekly by in/scripts/build_in_county_officials.py. A winner is not a sitting member: Indiana fills a vacancy by party caucus, which no result records, and the card says so. Every seat in the county is listed because neither body's district lines are drawn yet. Marion County's legislative body is the Indianapolis City-County Council, so its card names the council's 25 members and the Mayor of Indianapolis from the 2023 municipal general instead (in/scripts/build_in_city_officials.py).

layers.label: Indiana House District
layers.rank_note: 100 House districts — the finest political tiling this instance ships today

source.answers: The Indiana House district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (state lower chamber, field SLDL), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 100 features, measured 2026-09-29.

source.people: NO ROSTER SHIPS IN THIS CHANGE — the same gap as the Senate layer (in-general-assembly-roster); the card names the district and links the chamber's own directory.

layers.label: County Council District
layers.rank_note: 241 districts in 55 counties: four per county, and Indianapolis's 25 City-County Council districts

source.answers: Which county council district contains the point, and who won that district's seat and the county's three at-large seats; in Marion County, the Indianapolis City-County Council district and its member.

boundary.label: Indiana Geographic Information Office — Administrative Boundaries of Indiana, layer 4 (CountyCouncilPolygon), each county's own council districts, joined into one shape per district, clipped to the county and shipped with the app by in/scripts/build_in_council_districts.py; 56 counties file, 55 are drawn (Clay files three of its four districts), measured 2026-10-15.

source.people: The district's council member and the county's at-large members, each the winner of that seat's most recent election in the Indiana Election Division's certified results (in-county-councils.json; for Marion County, the 2023 municipal general in in-city-officials.json). A winner is not a sitting member: Indiana fills a vacancy by party caucus, and the card says so. Boone County's District 3 seat is titled "Dist 36" in the results, so its card does not guess which member holds it.
source.applies: Indiana — the 55 counties whose council districts the state's mapping office publishes in full. In the other 37 the card says the lines are not published, and the County card lists every council member.

layers.label: Court of Appeals District
layers.rank_note: the Court of Appeals' 3 geographic districts of whole counties, 31,411 km2 mean area, measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file — the largest districts Indiana carries below the state itself, three times a congressional district (10,470 km2)

source.answers: The Court of Appeals district covering the point, whose three judges stand for retention in that district alone.

boundary.label: Dissolved from the shipped county fabric (TIGERweb State_County layer 1) by in/scripts/build_in_appeals_districts.py, following the court's own district map (read 2026-10-16), the one place it publishes which counties are in each district; the Indiana Code that sets them is published only through a site that serves this project nothing it can read.
Court of Appeals of Indiana — its districts, and which judges stand for retention where

source.people: No judge is named yet; recorded as gap in-court-of-appeals-judges. The card says three of the court's fifteen judges come from the district and stand for retention only there.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 291 unified (K-12) districts, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive. Indiana runs NO elementary and NO secondary districts — both TIGERweb layers return ZERO features for STATE='18' (measured 2026-09-29) — so this instance ships ONE school layer where Michigan ships two, and the two empty layers are recorded drops rather than empty toggles

source.answers: The school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 291 features for Indiana, measured 2026-09-29. Layers 1 (SECONDARY) and 2 (ELEMENTARY) both return zero features for Indiana and are recorded drops — see docs/DATA_LAYER_GUIDEBOOK.md

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND THE CARD NAMES THE DISTRICT ONLY. Indiana school board members are elected — the Election Division certifies a School Board Member office category, whose own description says most members are elected and some are appointed — and the certified returns name 742 of them, but this change ships no roster and no districted geometry exists statewide, so nobody is named. Recorded as gap in-school-board-members.
source.applies: Indiana — statewide. The 291 unified districts are the whole of the state's school-district fabric.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 807 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping Indiana (882 counting the 75 that only touch its line), in a mirrored tile archive, measured 2026-10-17 — about 107 km2 mean, between a county and a township, which is where a ZIP ranks in Indiana and is NOT where it ranks in Michigan

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='18', in Esri's own {xmin,ymin,xmax,ymax} shape; 1,491 features fall in this instance's envelope and 882 actually intersect Indiana, measured 2026-09-29 against the state's own TIGERweb polygon

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Indiana — the 882 ZCTAs that intersect the state. A point outside Indiana gets the layer's own empty note rather than a ZIP code.

layers.label: Township
layers.rank_note: 1,012 county-subdivision records tiling the state, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive — 1,004 are civil townships (LSADC 44), and the other eight are Census bookkeeping: four coextensive town records, one city record (Muncie), the Camp Atterbury unorganized territory, and two 'not defined' records, all measured 2026-09-29

source.answers: The civil township covering the point — in Indiana a real unit of government, not a Census construct.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / county subdivisions, layer 1, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 1,012 features for Indiana, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: The township trustee and the three-member township board, as elected at the November 2022 general, from the Indiana Election Division's certified results (in-township-officials.json): 973 trustees and 921 boards of the 1,004 civil townships. A township the results do not cover, including Marion County's five-member boards, says so on the card, and the names are election winners rather than a roster the township keeps. Recorded as gap in-township-officers.
source.applies: Indiana — statewide. The card distinguishes a civil township from the eight records that are Census bookkeeping rather than a government.

layers.label: Conservancy District
layers.rank_note: The 100 active conservancy districts on the Department of Natural Resources' map, pre-built with the app — 75.5 km2 mean area (median 4.44, largest 1,342), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a civil township, of which 1,012 tile the state, and larger than an Indianapolis Public Schools board district (41.6). Some overlap; together they cover 8.0% of the state, overlaps counted once.

source.answers: The conservancy district or districts covering the point — special districts a circuit court sets up, when property owners ask, to deal with flooding, drainage, sewers, water supply or a lake — and who sits on each one's board.

boundary.label: Indiana Department of Natural Resources — Conservancy Districts of Indiana, layer 54 on gisdata.in.gov: the 100 districts the map marks active, measured 2026-10-16, pre-built by in/scripts/build_in_conservancy_districts.py and shipped with the app. One district the department's 2026 directory lists, Hidden Hills, carries no status on the map and is not drawn. The layer states no licence.

source.people: Each board as the district reported it to the Department of Natural Resources for its 2026 directory, read by in/scripts/build_in_conservancy_directors.py: 465 people named and 6 seats vacant across 93 districts, with the telephone and e-mail the directory prints beside each person and each district's own (on the copy read 2026-10-17, 145 people with a telephone and 181 with an e-mail, 86 districts with a telephone and 83 with an e-mail). A value printed for two or more people, or equal to the district's own, is the district's and is not shown on a person. Six districts sent no list, and one on the map (Geist Reservoir) is not in the directory; the card says so for each rather than naming anyone. Staff a district hires (attorneys, engineers, managers, operators) are not shown, and the home towns and addresses the directory gives are never carried.
source.applies: Indiana — wherever a district has been set up; most of the state is in none.

layers.label: School Board District
layers.rank_note: The 5 districts the Indianapolis Public Schools board is elected from, pre-built from the City of Indianapolis's layer — 41.6 km2 mean area (median 40.0), measured 2026-10-16 on the drawn file: smaller on average than a civil township, of which 1,012 tile the state, larger than a voting precinct (18.40)

source.answers: The district the Indianapolis Public Schools board elects a member from. Everywhere else in Indiana the card says this map draws no other board's districts yet.

boundary.label: City of Indianapolis and Marion County — School Board Districts, layer 9 of its OpenData_Political map service: the five Indianapolis Public Schools districts, measured 2026-10-16, pre-built by in/scripts/build_in_school_board_districts.py and shipped with the app. The same layer draws residence districts for the Lawrence and Washington township boards, which are not drawn because the whole township votes for every seat. The service states no licence.

source.people: NO NAMES YET. No list of the Indianapolis Public Schools board's members has been read, so the card names no one rather than guessing; recorded as gap in-school-board-members.
source.applies: Indianapolis Public Schools, in Marion County. The 2022 and 2024 results point to about forty other Indiana boards electing some members by district, and no statewide map of their districts is published (gap in-school-board-districts).

layers.label: Voting Precinct
layers.rank_note: 5,121 precincts tiling the state, pre-built from IndianaMap's 2026 layer — 18.40 km2 mean area, land and water (median 2.50), measured 2026-10-15 on the drawn file: about five to a civil township, since 1,012 county-subdivision records tile the same ground, and larger on average than a city or town (12.65 km2 of land)

source.answers: The voting precinct containing the point — where a reader votes and how their ballots are reported.

boundary.label: Indiana Geographic Information Office (IndianaMap) — Voting District Boundaries 2026, which the item says was obtained from the Indiana General Assembly and the Indiana Election Division in June 2026; 5,121 features, pre-built for the state by in/scripts/build_in_precincts.py and shipped with the app. A precinct a county changed after June 2026 is not shown, which the card says. The item names no licence, only a limitation of warranties.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, and none is missing. A precinct elects nobody — it is an election-administration unit, not a district with a representative — so the card says that rather than leaving a reader to wonder which name is absent.

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 566 incorporated places, from TIGERweb, drawn from a mirrored tile archive — 446 towns, 119 cities and the one 'Indianapolis city (balance)' record the consolidated Marion County city-county government produces, measured 2026-09-29

source.answers: The incorporated city or town covering the point, if any — and which of the two it is, because in Indiana that changes what governs the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places / incorporated places, layer 4, copied into a tile archive served from this site, re-fetched from the Census weekly; 566 features for Indiana, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: The mayor and council of all 39 places over 25,000 people. For 36 of them (all 33 cities and three of six towns) each name is the winner of that seat's most recent election in the Indiana Election Division's certified results (the 2023 municipal general), dated to that election; a winner is not a sitting member, because Indiana fills a vacancy by party caucus, and the card says so. Plainfield, Brownsburg and Schererville are towns where an uncontested seat is on no ballot, so their councils are read from each town's own council page and dated to the read. Rebuilt weekly by in/scripts/build_in_city_officials.py. Smaller places are not named yet. Recorded as gap in-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Indiana — statewide, all 566 incorporated places. 'Indianapolis city (balance)' is the Census record for the part of the consolidated Indianapolis–Marion County government outside its included towns, not a separate municipality.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: 650 police-station points in Indiana's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, ranked with the other point layers rather than by feature area

source.answers: The three nearest police station BUILDINGS to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the shared paged loader (no builder script, no committed data/app file). Public domain. 650 points in this instance's envelope, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district.
source.applies: Indiana — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes (449 of the 650 are in Indiana; the rest Illinois 123, Kentucky 75, Ohio 2 and Michigan 1, measured 2026-09-29 on the app's own metro_bbox envelope).

layers.label: Fire & EMS Station
layers.rank_note: 1,758 fire and EMS station points in Indiana's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer

source.answers: The three nearest fire or EMS station BUILDINGS to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 51 (Fire and EMS Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the shared paged loader. Public domain. 1,758 points in this instance's envelope, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a station is a facility. Indiana's fire and EMS RESPONSE AREAS are a different thing, filed by the state's NG911 programme, and ship as their own layers in a later change.
source.applies: Indiana — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes (1,245 of the 1,758 are in Indiana; the rest Illinois 304, Kentucky 201 and Ohio 8, measured 2026-09-29 on the app's own metro_bbox envelope).

layers.label: Post Office
layers.rank_note: 1,012 post-office points in Indiana's envelope, live from the USGS National Map (no data/app file) — a nearest-3 proximity layer, so it is ranked last with the other point layers

source.answers: The three nearest post offices to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 38 (Post Offices), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the shared paged loader. Public domain. 1,012 points in this instance's envelope, measured 2026-09-29

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a post office is a federal facility, not an elected district.
source.applies: Indiana — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes (716 of the 1,012 are in Indiana; the rest Illinois 182, Kentucky 107 and Ohio 5, plus one record each the publisher places in Maine and Iowa, measured 2026-09-29 on the app's own metro_bbox envelope).

layers.label: Tribal Government
layers.rank_note: Tribal land — Indiana has 1 piece, 0.931 km² of the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi's off-reservation trust land, MEASURED by scripts/build_tribal_areas.py; the rest of that trust land, 8% of which lies in Indiana, is in Michigan. Drawn above cities and towns, which are larger. Drawn although no district is drawn on this land, by Adam's ruling of 2026-09-30: a government answers for that ground, so a reader who clicks it should be told which one.

source.answers: Whether this address is on tribal land, and which nation's government answers for it — Indiana has one such area, the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi's.

boundary.label: US Census Bureau TIGERweb AIANNHA, current vintage — federal reservations and off-reservation trust land, shipped with the app

source.people: The council, from the Pokagon Band's own published council page, read weekly by scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py and dated on the card — the same read the Michigan card uses. The government, its seat and its website come from the Bureau of Indian Affairs' tribal leaders directory (data/bia-tribal-governments.json); the land is joined to the government by this project's own data/tribal-government-join.json.
source.applies: Indiana — one area, a piece of the Pokagon Band's trust land near South Bend. Almost every point in the state is on no tribal land.

anchor_point.note: the Indiana Statehouse, downtown Indianapolis (Marion County)

negative_point.note: downtown Louisville, Kentucky — south of the Ohio River, whose north bank is the Indiana line, and inside permalink_gate's minLat (37.60) so the point is still selectable; measured to miss all four ANCHOR layers (the live TIGERweb fabric layers are deliberately not anchors — an anchor must answer with the network down) KENTUCKY WENT LIVE ON 2026-09-30 AND NOW COVERS THIS POINT, so the two checks that put it at the map's CENTRE refused ../fleet-outlines.json until 2026-10-13, when panning stopped switching apps; neither refuses anything now, because a selection the app makes itself never leaves. The point itself is unchanged: it is still outside this instance and still misses all four anchor layers, and the gate reaches uncovered ground in Ohio if it ever needs to move. Check 1a2 is where this instance asserts fleet routing, and Louisville moved there from its uncovered case to a Kentucky routing case the same day.

geometry.note: The whole-Indiana-state outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from all 92 counties' TIGERweb State_County layer-1 geometry by in/scripts/build_metro_outline.py (METRO_COUNTY_FIPS = every county; DISPATCH_COUNTY_FIPS empty — no layer is county-keyed yet). Indiana is 2-band coverage: every layer answers statewide, so there is no wider region band.
Every county, pre-built from TIGERweb State_County layer 1.
U.S. House districts, pre-built from TIGERweb Legislative layer 0 (field CD120 — the 120th Congress).
Indiana Senate districts, pre-built by in/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).
Indiana House districts, pre-built by in/scripts/build_legislative_boundaries.py (2,000-point agreement gate).

Indiana's tribal land (scripts/build_tribal_areas.py) — one piece of the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi's trust land, which crosses from Michigan. The floor and the ceiling are equal because that is what the Census publishes inside the state on the current vintage, measured 2026-10-10; a change in either direction is a change in the Census's own map and wants reading rather than a widened bound.

Every Indiana voting precinct, pre-built by in/scripts/build_in_precincts.py through scripts/statewide_precincts.py from IndianaMap's 2026 layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m, the smallest of 4, 8 and 12 m that keeps the file at or under 2.5 MB gzipped; a 6,000-point agreement gate, measured 99.98% with zero overlaps; an exact 5,121 count on the fetch and the drawn file). 7.1 MB, 1.48 MB gzipped, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

County council districts in 55 counties and Indianapolis's 25 City-County Council districts, from the Indiana Geographic Information Office's CountyCouncilPolygon layer, built by in/scripts/build_in_council_districts.py.

The five Indianapolis Public Schools board districts, pre-built by in/scripts/build_in_school_board_districts.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the City of Indianapolis's layer (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; a 400-point agreement gate, measured 100.00% with zero overlaps). 24 KB, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

The Court of Appeals' 1st, 2nd and 3rd Districts, dissolved from the county fabric by in/scripts/build_in_appeals_districts.py following the court's own district map; the 4th and 5th are statewide and not drawn.

Indiana's 100 active conservancy districts, pre-built by in/scripts/build_in_conservancy_districts.py through scripts/published_district_layers.py from the Department of Natural Resources' map (Douglas-Peucker at 4 m; an 18,800-point agreement gate over each court's districts, measured 99.99% with zero overlaps; an exact 100 count). 264 KB, fetched only when a reader switches the layer on.

rosters.note: All 9 U.S. House members, rebuilt weekly by CI from unitedstates/congress-legislators.

Every county commissioner in 91 counties (Marion's body is the Indianapolis City-County Council, in in-city-officials.json), each the winner of that seat's most recent certified general, built by in/scripts/build_in_county_officials.py from the Indiana Election Division's results archive.
Every county council member in 91 counties (Marion excluded), from the same certified results and the same builder.

The mayor and council of 36 of Indiana's 39 places over 25,000 people, Indianapolis's City-County Council among them, each the winner of that seat's most recent certified municipal general, built by in/scripts/build_in_city_officials.py from the Indiana Election Division's results archive.

The trustee and township board of 987 of Indiana's 1,004 civil townships, keyed by Census county-subdivision id, each the winner of the most recent certified township election (2022), built by in/scripts/build_in_township_officials.py from the Indiana Election Division's results archive.

The board of each conservancy district as it reported it to the Department of Natural Resources for its 2026 directory, keyed by the district's id on the map, built by in/scripts/build_in_conservancy_directors.py: names, roles, and the telephone and e-mail the directory prints beside each person and for each district, 99 districts. The directory is published once a year, so this is rebuilt by hand when a new edition appears (in/WATCH.md).
The recorded gaps this instance ships, generated by scripts/build_coverage_gaps.py from the guidebook's gaps block.

The council of every Indiana nation whose council is carried, keyed by the Census AIANNH code of its land — scripts/build_tribal_areas.py --rosters from data/tribal-councils.json, which scripts/tribal_council_scraper.py re-reads weekly (update-tribal-councils.yml, listed in the Wisconsin worksheet because one root workflow belongs to one instance). Merged onto tribal-areas.json by the layer's loader, so the land stays cache-first and the names network-first.
